sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about Iceland.
Iceland is a cold, beautiful,
and peaceful country in Northern Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Iceland?
Iceland is an island country in the North Atlantic Ocean.
It is between Greenland and Norway, near the Arctic Circle.
It is far from other countries, but it is a part of Europe.
What is the capital city of Iceland?
The capital city is Reykjavik.
It is the largest city in Iceland.
It has colorful houses, hot springs,
modern buildings, and art.
Other towns include Akirari, in the North,
Haffnerfjørther, Salfos, and Isafjørther.
How many people live in Iceland?
Only about 400,000 people live in Iceland.
It is a small population for a big island.
Most people live near the coast,
especially around Reykjavik.
The center of the island is mostly uninhabited nature.
What language do people speak in Iceland?
People speak Icelandic.
It is the official language.
It is an old language, very close to ancient Norse.
Most Icelanders also speak English very well,
and some speak Danish or other languages.
What is the weather like in Iceland?
Iceland has a cold climate, but not as cold as you might think.
Because of the ocean, winters are mild and summers are cool.
Winter, cold, dark, and snowy.
Summer, cool and bright with very long days.
In June and July, the sun stays up almost all night.
In winter, it is dark for most of the day.
What does Iceland look like?
Iceland is full of amazing nature.
Volcanoes, glaciers, waterfalls, hot springs, lava fields.
There are also geysers, hot water that shoots out of the ground.
You can see the northern lights in the sky in winter.
What animals live in Iceland?
Iceland has sheep, horses, and cows on farms.
Arctic foxes in the wild, puffins, seagulls, and other seabirds.
In the ocean, whales, seals, and fish.
There are no snakes or large wild animals on land.
What do people eat in Iceland?
Icelandic food is simple, fresh, and often sea-based.
People eat fish like cotton salmon, lamin dairy products,
rye bread, potatoes, and vegetables.
Popular dishes, plockfisker, fish and potatoes and sauce,
skier, a yogurt-like dairy snack, lamb soup,
flat caca, flat rye bread with butter or smoked meat.
Heartfisker, dried fish, sometimes eaten as a snack.
What do people drink in Iceland?
People drink water, very clean and fresh from nature.
Milk, coffee, and tea, fruit juice.
Adults may drink beer, wine, or brenovine, a local spirit.
Hot drinks are popular in cold weather.
What is life like in Iceland?
Life in Iceland is quiet, safe, and organized.
People enjoy reading books, swimming in hot pools,
hiking and camping, music and arts,
spending time with family.
The country is known for its education,
equality, and clean energy.
What are some holidays and traditions in Iceland?
National Day, June 17, Christmas with 13 U-Lads
instead of Santa Claus.
New Year's Eve, with lots of fireworks.
First day of summer, a spring holiday.
Thoroblot, a winter festival with traditional foods.
Icelanders also enjoy music festivals and literature events.
Some fun facts about Iceland.
Iceland uses 100% renewable energy for electricity and heating.
There are more sheep than people in the country.
Iceland has no army.
The Icelandic horse is a special small horse with a unique gate.
People believe in elves and hidden people in old stories.
Now you know many things about Iceland.
You know where it is, what people speak and what they eat.
You learned about the weather, nature, and culture.
Great job.
I am Emily.
Goodbye, or as they say in Icelandic, bless.
